'''Alec Peters''' (born April 13, 1995) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] player for [[Valparaiso University]], where he was an [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in 2017.

Peters, a 6'9" [[small forward]] from [[Washington, Illinois]], selected [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]] over larger-conference school like [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Doster| first = Adam | title = Beyond the Horizon  | work = [[Sports Illustrated]] | date = March 7, 2016 | url = http://www.si.com/vault/2016/03/15/beyond-horizon | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref> He immediately became the focus of the team's offense as a freshman, having an eventful season in adjusting to opponent defensive attention and the distraction of serious storms causing destruction in his hometown.<ref>{{cite web | last = Oren| first = Paul | title = Valparaiso freshman Peters working through six weeks of struggles| work = [[The Times of Northwest Indiana]] | date = January 17, 2014 | url = http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/basketball/college/valparaiso-freshman-peters-working-through-six-weeks-of-struggles/article_e2a50369-e121-5c23-9f54-0eb2e049c6b1.html | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = Norlander| first = Matt | title = Midwest tornadoes hit home for Valpo star freshman Alec Peters  | work = [[CBSSports.com]] | date = November 20, 2013 | url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24250385/midwest-tornadoes-hit-home-for-valpo-star-freshman-alec-peters | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref> As a sophomore, Peters settled into a starring role, averaging 16.8 [[points per game|points]] and 6.7 [[rebounds per game]]. At the conclusion of the season, he was named first-team All-[[Horizon League]].<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Five Crusaders Honored by Horizon League  | work = [[Valparaiso Crusaders]] | date = March 2, 2015 | url = http://www.valpoathletics.com/mbasketball/news/2014-15/14430/five-crusaders-honored-by-horizon-league/#.V7zlnU2V-XI | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref> In the [[2015 Horizon League Men's Basketball Tournament|2015 Horizon League Tournament]], Peters was named tournament MVP in leading the Crusaders to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web | last = | first = | title = From Washington, Manual to NCAAs: Alec Peters, Lawrence Alexander lead teams to tourney titles | work = [[Journal Star (Peoria)|Peoria Journal Star]] | date = March 11, 2015 | url = http://www.pjstar.com/article/20150311/Sports/150319804 | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref>

In his junior season, Peters gained more of a national reputation. He averaged 18.4 points and 8.4 rebounds per game and led the Crusaders to the [[2016 National Invitation Tournament]] final, where they lost to [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]]. At the close of the season, Peters took advantage of looser [[NBA draft]] eligibility rules to declare for the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web | last = Osipoff| first = Michael| title = Valparaiso's Alec Peters decides to declare for NBA Draft — for now | work = [[Chicago Tribune]] | date = April 7, 2016 | url = http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-ptb-mens-basketball-valparaiso-alec-peters-st-0408-20160407-story.html | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref> He ultimately chose to withdraw his name and after speculation that he might transfer, he opted to return to Valparaiso for his senior year in 2016–17.<ref>{{cite web | last = Dauster| first = Rob| title = Alec Peters withdraws from NBA Draft, will he transfer? | work = [[NBCSports.com]] | date = May 26, 2016 | url = http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2016/05/26/alec-peters-withdraws-from-nba-draft-will-he-transfer/ | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last = Evans| first = Andrew| title = Alec Peters' return to Valparaiso sends shockwaves through the Horizon League | work = [[SBNation.com]] | date = June 2, 2016 | url = http://www.midmajormadness.com/2016/6/2/11826016/alec-peters-return-valparaiso-crusaders-horizon-league-impact | accessdate = August 23, 2016}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]], Peters was named the preseason Horizon League Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Horizon League Announces Men's Basketball Preseason Awards|url=http://www.horizonleague.org/blog/horizon-league-mens-basketball-preseason-awards|accessdate=January 2, 2017|work=[[Horizon League]]|date=October 6, 2016}}</ref> He surpassed the 2,000 career point mark in a December 28 game against [[Chicago State Cougars men's basketball|Chicago State]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Peters Reaches 2,000 Career Points in Crusaders’ Win Over Chicago State|url=http://www.valpoathletics.com/mbasketball/news/2016-17/16001/peters-reaches-2000-career-points-in-crusaders-win-over-chicago-state/#.WGrMzcs8KhA|accessdate=January 2, 2017|work=[[Valparaiso Crusaders]]|date=December 28, 2016}}</ref> At the end of the regular season, Peters was officially named the [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]].
